Asturian

Etymology

From Vulgar Latin *plovere, from Classical Latin pluere.

Pronunciation

  • IPA(key): /ʎoˈbeɾ/ [ʎoˈβ̞eɾ]
  • Rhymes: -eɾ
  • Syllabification: llo‧ver

Verb

llover

  1. (impersonal) to rain

Related terms

  • lloviu, lluvia
  • lluviosu

Further reading

  • “llover”, in Diccionariu de la llingua asturiana [Dictionary of the Asturian Language] (in Asturian), 1st edition, Academy of the Asturian Language [Asturian: Academia de la Llingua Asturiana], 2000, →ISBN
  • García Arias, Xosé Lluis (2002–2004), “llover”, in Diccionario general de la lengua asturiana [General Dictionary of the Asturian Language] (overall work in Spanish), Editorial Prensa Asturiana, →ISBN

Spanish

Etymology

Inherited from Vulgar Latin *plovere, from Classical Latin pluere. Compare Portuguese chover.

Pronunciation

 
  • IPA(key): /ʝoˈbeɾ/ [ɟ͡ʝoˈβ̞eɾ]
  • IPA(key): /ʝoˈbeɾ/ [ɟ͡ʝoˈβ̞eɾ] (Spain, most of Latin America, Equatorial Guinea)
  • IPA(key): /ʎoˈbeɾ/ [ʎoˈβ̞eɾ] (rustic northern Spain, northern and central Andes Mountains (except central Ecuador), Bolivia, Paraguay, northeastern Argentina, Philippines)
  • IPA(key): /ʃoˈbeɾ/ [ʃoˈβ̞eɾ] (Buenos Aires and environs)
  • IPA(key): /ʒoˈbeɾ/ [ʒoˈβ̞eɾ] (central Ecuador, Santiago del Estero and environs, elsewhere in Pampas and southern Argentina, Uruguay)

  • Audio (Colombia):(file)
  • Rhymes: -eɾ
  • Syllabification: llo‧ver

Verb

llover (impersonal, third-person singular present llueve, third-person singular preterite llovió, past participle llovido)

  1. (intransitive, impersonal) to rain
    Hyponym: lloviznar
    Coordinate term: nevar (“to snow”)
    Llueve. ― It’s raining.
    Parece que va a llover.
    It looks like it's going to rain.
    Ojalá llueva.
    I hope it rains.
    Dejó de llover.
    It stopped raining.
    Deja que llueva.
    Let it rain.
    Espera a que llueva.
    Wait until it rains.

Usage notes

  • Usually only used in the third person, except in figurative usage:
    2006, Andrés Trapiello, “Lluevo”, in El volador de cometas: antología poética‎:
    Lluevo en esta ciudad
    envuelto en frío, en aguacero, en noche,
    I rain in this city
    Wrapped in cold, in downpour, in night,
